analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (October 23, 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell -0.5% on the week to 7,623.68 as investors digested the start of mega-cap tech earnings, a macro backdrop of oil up and rates down, and a debate over the durability of the AI infrastructure trade. AI-At-Risk, AI Software and Alternative Asset Managers outperformed. Goldminers, Copper and IPPs underperformed.
Prime book: US equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (4 of last 5, -0.9 SDs 1-year). Single stocks drove it with long-and-short sales, the largest de-grossing since late July.
Single stocks were 77% of total net selling and were net sold for a 5th straight week. Macro products (index and ETF) were 23% of net selling, with short sales outpacing long buys about 2 to 1.

Industrials was among the most net sold sectors. HFs net sold the group for a 2nd straight week (7 of last 8) at the fastest pace in more than 6 months (-1.8 SDs 1-year). Industrials long/short ratio is 1.67, in the 2nd percentile vs. the past year.

Staples and Real Estate were by far the most net bought sectors, which the desk reads as a defensive posture. Real Estate net buying was the largest in more than 5 years (+2.4 SDs). Staples net buying was the largest since Jul '25 (+1.8 SDs).

US L/S gross leverage rose 2.2 pts to 216.1% (64th percentile one-year). Net leverage fell 0.3 pts to 43.4% (0th percentile five-year). The fundamental long/short ratio fell 0.7% to 1.503 (0th percentile five-year).

Shares desk: LOs and HFs were moderate net sellers, most acutely in tech. About $20bn of net TMT selling over 2 weeks across all client types and channels, approaching the $23bn over 2 weeks seen in the July AI selling episode. Little rotation into defensives this week, unlike the prior week.

Futures: Managed Money initiated significant long call positions in Brent through mid-October. Of the $2.3bn in new gross longs from Oct 6-13, 32% were calls. Another ~$1bn was bought through Oct 20. Brent 3-month 25 delta put-call skew still cheapened, and dealers appear incrementally shorter gamma to the upside.

Long bond futures completed a round trip from the mid-September selloff. December Ultra-Bond futures are up 6% from the 10/7 low, a 40bp move in implied forward yield on the CTD vs. about 15bp in 2y yields. The desk links the move to AI weakness (GS AI basket -16% from 10/7) and HY CDX spreads 26bp wider.

Elevated rate vols may dampen risk parity demand for bonds (RP models show bond length still unwinding). Negative correlation with risk assets raises bonds' diversification value and could draw real money buyers. TY put-call skew turned negative.

Derivatives: capitulation and de-grossing on Thursday on AI financing worries and geopolitical escalation. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had one of its largest drops on record, to its lowest since April of last year. Friday volume was -21% vs 5d avg and -33% vs 100d avg.

Vol of vol is at its highest since April (83rd percentile, 3-year lookback). The NDX-SPX implied vol spread blew out to the 98th percentile vs 5 years. Thursday's widening was the second largest in 5 years. SPX skew was bid, but flows showed less reach for downside protection, which the desk attributes to historically low net exposure.

EWZ 1-month normalized put-call skew is at all-time highs ahead of the Brazil election. Desk flows were decisively bullish, with interest in EWZ calls and call spreads and in GSBZRATE for higher beta.

Baskets desk: AI vs AI-At-Risk pair (GSPUARTI) is down about 13% YTD and the S&P ex AI index (SPXXAI) has passed the S&P 500 YTD. The desk says this is a HF deleveraging episode where short-term stops matter more than medium-term value, and recommends buying the dip selectively in AI: Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber.

Baskets desk: cyclicals face slowing growth, higher oil, tighter financial conditions and a tightening cycle. It recommends GSXUCYCL as a funding short alongside Low Quality expressions (NPTC, LOWQ, DEBT).

TMT specialists: NDX -80bps on the week (GS TMT Broad AI Basket -4.1%, TMT Mo' Basket -7.8%). Debate centers on the driver of price action (oil, earnings sell-the-news in META, LRCX, TTMI, WDC, positioning) and on what would turn the story. Investors cite the election, easing macro headwinds or AI datapoints. Appetite is rising for non-AI, idiosyncratic TMT ideas.

Financials: outperformed the market despite weak sentiment. Blackstone's caution on real estate was followed by a +8% rally in the stock against crowded shorts. A barbell of high quality defensives (P&C insurance, card networks, senior housing REITs) and cheap value risk-on (regional banks, mid cap payments, lodging REITs, life insurance) outperformed. Life insurance began to leak late in the week on credit spreads and investment portfolios.

Industrials and Materials: Industrials -150bps vs the broader market -30bps. Materials +125bps on geopolitical tension keeping inflation fears and commodity prices elevated. Movers: BMI +20% (short covering), EQPT +19% (pre-announced beat and raise), ALLE and POOL +15% (better than feared), AVEX -28% (Navy product scrutiny), CRS -25% (rare miss and guide down), FPS -22% (AI/data center weakness, abrupt CFO departure).

Healthcare: earnings had mixed updates (ABT lower organic guide, ISRG light US procedures, DHR respiratory guide cut, TMO). Price action followed pre-set theme playbooks. Tools/CROs benefit from AI drug-discovery themes, Medtech sees recovery buying, Managed Care trades around the midterms. MRNA fell 17.5% and MRK 1.8% on Thursday after the intismeran data leak, even though the 0.58 hazard ratio cleared the <0.6 bar, with bears re-engaging.

Next week: S&P implied move through 10/30 is 1.80%. Central banks decide (FOMC and BOC Wed, ECB Thu, BOJ Fri). 44% of S&P market cap reports Q3 earnings (MSFT, GOOG, NOW, KLAC Wed, AMZN, INTC Thu, plus SNDK, STX, SEC/Hynix, ORCL analyst day). Brazil election results are due Sunday night.
